title: The Cookbook Code
teaser: A sapphire brooch disappears from a tea room. Under the sugar bowl, a note made of nothing but numbers.

booklet.briefing:
Mrs. Abernathy has taken tea at the Copper Kettle every Saturday for twenty years. On Saturday she wore her late husband's sapphire brooch pinned to her coat. When she put the coat back on at 3:30, the brooch was gone.

That evening the cleaner found a slip of green paper under the sugar bowl on table 6. It was covered in numbers, in groups of three.

On table 6, as on every table, sits a copy of the tea room's favourite book: Grandma Pell's Kitchen. Mr. Foxy thinks the two might be related.
rules: The brooch was taken from Mrs. Abernathy's coat between 2:00 pm and 3:30 pm, while the coat hung on the stand by the door.
Each number group in the note is page.line.word in Grandma Pell's Kitchen.

suspects.name: Ollie Vance
suspects.description: Ponytail, quick smile. Works the front of the tea room with an order pad in his apron.
suspects.motive: Owes rent and has asked for extra shifts.
suspects.statement: I took Mrs. A's coat and fetched it for her afterwards, same as every week. I never touched the brooch.

suspects.name: Priya Nair
suspects.description: Works the back half of the room. Also carries an order pad.
suspects.motive: Was told off by Mrs. Abernathy for slow service last month.
suspects.statement: I served tables 7 to 12 all afternoon. I didn't go near the coat stand.

suspects.name: Sam Cole
suspects.description: Bakes the scones and cakes in the kitchen behind the counter.
suspects.motive: Has been warned that the Copper Kettle may close and he'll lose his job.
suspects.statement: I was in the kitchen all day. You can't leave scones in the oven.

suspects.name: Leonard Pell-Kaplan
suspects.description: Grandson of the real Grandma Pell, who wrote the cookbook. Knows it by heart.
suspects.statement: I sat at table 2 by the window with the crossword. I've no need to steal brooches; I buy them.

evidence.title: Grandma Pell's Kitchen, page 9: Scones
evidence.body:
Line 1: The secret of a good scone is cold butter

Line 2: and a light hand. Never twist the cutter.

Line 3: Brush the tops with milk, not egg,

Line 4: and bake in a hot oven until golden.

Line 5: Keep them in a tin lined with a napkin.

Line 6: They are best eaten on the day.

Line 2: Stir it slowly over gentle heat,

Line 3: under no circumstances let it boil.

Line 4: Strain into warm jars and seal at once.

Line 5: Spread it thick on hot toast on Sunday.

Line 6: A spoonful in the cake makes it sing.

evidence.title: Order pads
evidence.body:
Each waiter has their own numbered green pad and keeps it in their apron pocket all shift.

Ollie Vance: sheets 0401 to 0500. Priya Nair: sheets 0501 to 0600.

Sam and Mrs. Dunmore, the manager, don't use order pads.

evidence.title: Pencil rubbing
evidence.body:
The top sheet left in Ollie's pad is 0458. Rubbing a pencil lightly over it shows the pressed-in marks of numbers written on the sheet above it: 14.3.5   22.1.3   9.4.3 ...

Priya's pad: the top sheet is 0539. A rubbing shows the marks of an order for two cream teas, nothing else.

evidence.title: Mrs. Abernathy
evidence.body:
“The young man with the ponytail took my coat at two and hung it up, and he brought it back to me at half past three. The brooch was definitely on it when I came in, I touched it at the door for luck.”

“Mr. Pell-Kaplan didn't leave his window seat. He kept asking me for a seven-letter word for 'sneak thief'.”

evidence.title: The shelf behind the counter
evidence.body:
A row of old display teapots on a high shelf behind the counter. Only staff go behind the counter.

One of them, an old blue teapot, is never used for serving.

solution.explanation: Ollie Vance unpinned the brooch when he hung up Mrs. Abernathy's coat, then hid it inside the old blue display teapot behind the counter, where nobody ever looks. He coded a message for a friend using the cookbook on table 6: IT IS IN THE OLD BLUE TEAPOT. COLLECT SUNDAY AT NOON. He tore the sheet off his own order pad, and the sheet underneath kept the dents of every number.

chain.step: Decoded with page.line.word: IT IS IN THE OLD BLUE TEAPOT. COLLECT SUNDAY AT NOON.
The blue teapot is on a staff-only shelf behind the counter, and the brooch was inside it.
The note is sheet 0457 from Ollie's pad, and his sheet 0458 has the same numbers pressed into it.
Ollie took the coat at 2:00 and brought it back at 3:30, so he had the chance to unpin the brooch.
